# testhta

**Automated Verification and Unit Testing for Health Economic and HTA
Models in R**

`testhta` provides a practical, software-engineering-inspired framework
for applying **automated verification** (unit, integration, and system
testing) to health economic and health technology assessment (HTA)
models in R. Built around the [`testthat`](https://testthat.r-lib.org/)
package, `testhta` accompanies the tutorial paper *“Automated
Verification for Health Economic Models in R: A Hands-On Tutorial”*
(Green, Gallardo, & Lamrock, 2026) and includes a complete 3-state
discrete-time cohort Markov model case study and verification test
suite.

Ensuring HTA model quality should not rely solely on ad-hoc console
checks or manual spreadsheet audits. `testhta` makes verification
automated, reproducible, and transparent—proactively catching silent
logic bugs before they influence reimbursement decisions.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Key Features

- 🧪 **Custom Verification Expectations**: High-level wrapper
  expectations
  ([`check_model_qalys()`](https://validate-hta.github.io/testhta/reference/check_model_qalys.md),
  [`check_model_costs()`](https://validate-hta.github.io/testhta/reference/check_model_costs.md),
  [`check_model_le()`](https://validate-hta.github.io/testhta/reference/check_model_le.md),
  [`check_model_le_pp()`](https://validate-hta.github.io/testhta/reference/check_model_le_pp.md))
  to verify model outputs against expected boundary values.
- 🔄 **Relational Model Comparators**: Compare outputs across parameter
  configurations using
  [`compare_model_runs()`](https://validate-hta.github.io/testhta/reference/compare_model_runs.md)
  (e.g., verifying that positive discounting reduces future QALYs and
  costs, or that removing intervention costs reduces the ICER).
- 🔗 **Modular Helper Interface**: Isolate model internals from test
  scripts using getters
  ([`get_qalys()`](https://validate-hta.github.io/testhta/reference/get_qalys.md),
  [`get_costs()`](https://validate-hta.github.io/testhta/reference/get_costs.md),
  [`get_le()`](https://validate-hta.github.io/testhta/reference/get_le.md),
  [`get_le_pp()`](https://validate-hta.github.io/testhta/reference/get_le_pp.md),
  [`get_icer()`](https://validate-hta.github.io/testhta/reference/get_icer.md))
  and pipe-friendly setters
  ([`set_discount_rate()`](https://validate-hta.github.io/testhta/reference/set_discount_rate.md),
  [`set_time_horizon()`](https://validate-hta.github.io/testhta/reference/set_time_horizon.md),
  [`set_costs()`](https://validate-hta.github.io/testhta/reference/set_costs.md),
  [`set_utilities()`](https://validate-hta.github.io/testhta/reference/set_utilities.md),
  [`set_p_matrix()`](https://validate-hta.github.io/testhta/reference/set_p_matrix.md))
  alongside the
  [`run_model()`](https://validate-hta.github.io/testhta/reference/run_model.md)
  wrapper.
- ⚙️ **Executable Case Study & Scaffolding**: Includes the 3-state
  (`Asymptomatic`, `Progressive`, `Dead`) cohort Markov model
  ([`ce_markov()`](https://validate-hta.github.io/testhta/reference/ce_markov.md)),
  baseline parameters (`base_params`), end-to-end tutorial test script
  (`inst/tutorial-paper/run-model-tests.R`), and
  [`use_hta_unittests()`](https://validate-hta.github.io/testhta/reference/use_hta_unittests.md)
  to scaffold the test suite in your own project.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Installation

You can install the development version of `testhta` from GitHub:

``` r

# install.packages("devtools")
devtools::install_github("validate-hta/testhta")
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Quick Start: Build, Run, and Verify

Here is a basic example demonstrating how to run the cohort Markov model
case study and verify economic discounting logic.

### 1. Set Up and Run the Model

We use the package’s built-in baseline parameter list `base_params` (a
cohort of $`n = 1000`$ patients simulated over
$`n_{\text{cycles}} = 15`$ cycles at a $`3.5\%`$ discount rate) to
execute the cost-effectiveness model.

``` r

library(testhta)

# Load baseline parameters
data(base_params)

# Run the Markov simulation
results <- run_model(base_params)

# Extract key HTA outputs using getters
get_qalys(results)
#> without_drug    with_drug 
#>     8394.580     8981.496 

get_costs(results)
#> without_drug    with_drug 
#>      1147099      4865536 

get_le_pp(results)
#> without_drug    with_drug 
#>     12.06416     12.68332 

get_icer(results)
#> [1] 6335.546
```

### 2. Modify Parameters with Pipe Setters

Easily perform scenario analyses or sensitivity sweeps by piping
parameter modifications:

``` r

# Evaluate a 10-cycle time horizon with no discounting
scenario_results <- base_params |>
  set_time_horizon(10) |>
  set_discount_rate(0) |>
  run_model()

get_icer(scenario_results)
#> [1] 11902.39
```

### 3. Automated Verification Assertions

`testhta` integrates directly with `testthat` to express verification
checks from the HTA Test Registry (`T01`–`T12`):

``` r

library(testthat)

# T06: Verify that QALYs with standard discounting (3.5%) are strictly less
# than QALYs without discounting (0%)
compare_model_runs(
  extractor_fn = get_qalys,
  comparison_fn = expect_lt,
  params_1 = list(discount_rate = 0.035),
  params_2 = list(discount_rate = 0),
  data = base_params,
  label = "T06: Discounted should be less than undiscounted QALYs"
)
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## The HTA Verification Test Registry (T01 – T12)

The verification checks in `testhta` operationalize established HTA
quality-assurance frameworks (McCabe & Dixon, 2000; Tappenden &
Chilcott, 2014; Dasbach & Elbasha, 2017; CHEERS) across **12 core test
scenarios (`T01`–`T12`)** grouped into four domains:

- **Population Tests (`T01`–`T03`)**: Equal treatment effects yield
  equal LYGs and QALYs (`T01`); zero mortality yields life expectancy
  equal to the time horizon (`T02`); immediate 100% mortality yields
  life expectancy of 1 cycle (`T03`).
- **QALY Tests (`T04`–`T07`)**: Zero discount rate with living utilities
  $`= 1`$ yields total QALYs equal to LE (`T04`); living utilities
  $`= 1`$ yields QALY gains equal to LYGs (`T05`); positive discount
  rate reduces QALYs (`T06`); infinite/extreme discount rate reduces
  QALY gains after time 0 to zero (`T07`).
- **Cost Tests (`T08`–`T11`)**: Zero intervention cost reduces ICER
  (`T08`); increased intervention cost increases ICER (`T09`); zero
  vs. positive cost discounting (`T10`); infinite/extreme cost discount
  rate reduces costs after time 0 to zero (`T11`).
- **Input / PSA Tests (`T12`)**: Stochastic parameter samples drawn for
  Probabilistic Sensitivity Analysis (PSA) respect distribution domain
  boundaries (e.g., Beta utility draws strictly in $`(0, 1)`$ using
  [`withr::with_seed()`](https://withr.r-lib.org/reference/with_seed.html)).

For the complete test matrix, step-by-step code examples, custom
expectations, and AI-assisted testing workflows (`model-context.md`),
see the package vignettes: - [**Introduction to testhta & Case Study
Model**](https://validate-hta.github.io/testhta/articles/introduction.html) -
[**The HTA Verification Framework
(T01–T12)**](https://validate-hta.github.io/testhta/articles/verification-framework.html) -
[**R Test Code Examples (Discounting, Costs,
Population)**](https://validate-hta.github.io/testhta/articles/basic-tests.html) -
[**Custom Expectations & Stochastic PSA
Testing**](https://validate-hta.github.io/testhta/articles/validation-guide.html) -
[**Automating Tests & AI-Assisted
Verification**](https://validate-hta.github.io/testhta/articles/automating-hta-unit-tests.html)

## References

1.  **Green, N., Gallardo, D., & Lamrock, F.** (2026). Automated
    Verification for Health Economic Models in R: A Hands-On Tutorial.
    (See
    `inst/tutorial-paper/Validation_Testing_HE_Models_Tutorial.pdf`).
2.  **McCabe, C., & Dixon, S.** (2000). Testing the Validity of
    Cost-Effectiveness Models. *PharmacoEconomics*, 17(5), 501–513.
    <https://doi.org/10.2165/00019053-200017050-00007>
3.  **Tappenden, P., & Chilcott, J. B.** (2014). Avoiding and
    Identifying Errors and Other Threats to the Credibility of Health
    Economic Models. *PharmacoEconomics*, 32, 967–979.
    <https://doi.org/10.1007/s40273-014-0186-2>
4.  **Dasbach, E. J., & Elbasha, E. H.** (2017). Verification of
    Decision-Analytic Models for Health Economic Evaluations: An
    Overview. *PharmacoEconomics*, 35, 673–683.
    <https://doi.org/10.1007/s40273-017-0508-2>
5.  **Alarid-Escudero, F., et al.** (2019). A Need for Change! A Coding
    Framework for Improving Transparency in Decision Modeling.
    *PharmacoEconomics*, 37(11), 1329–1339.
    <https://doi.org/10.1007/s40273-019-00837-x>

# Package index

## Test Suite Generator

Scaffolding functions to automatically generate unit testing
infrastructure for HTA models.

- [`use_hta_unittests()`](https://validate-hta.github.io/testhta/reference/use_hta_unittests.md)
  : Generate Skeleton Unit Tests for HTA Models

## Model Validation & Verification Helpers

Exported assertion functions to write automated unit tests and check
model boundaries.

- [`run_model()`](https://validate-hta.github.io/testhta/reference/run_model.md)
  : Run Markov model with parameters and overrides
- [`check_model_qalys()`](https://validate-hta.github.io/testhta/reference/check_model_qalys.md)
  : Run model and check QALYs against an expected value
- [`check_model_costs()`](https://validate-hta.github.io/testhta/reference/check_model_costs.md)
  : Run model and check Costs against an expected value
- [`check_model_le()`](https://validate-hta.github.io/testhta/reference/check_model_le.md)
  : Run model and check Life Expectancy against an expected value
- [`check_model_le_pp()`](https://validate-hta.github.io/testhta/reference/check_model_le_pp.md)
  : Run model and check per-person Life Expectancy against an expected
  value
- [`compare_model_runs()`](https://validate-hta.github.io/testhta/reference/compare_model_runs.md)
  : Compare model outputs from two different parameter sets

## Model Setters & Getters

Helper functions to modify input parameters, query parameter matrices by
treatment arm, and extract outcomes during test execution.

- [`set_discount_rate()`](https://validate-hta.github.io/testhta/reference/set_discount_rate.md)
  : Set discount rate
- [`set_costs()`](https://validate-hta.github.io/testhta/reference/set_costs.md)
  : Set costs for a scenario
- [`set_p_matrix()`](https://validate-hta.github.io/testhta/reference/set_p_matrix.md)
  : Set transition probabilities for a scenario
- [`set_utilities()`](https://validate-hta.github.io/testhta/reference/set_utilities.md)
  : Set utilities for a scenario
- [`set_time_horizon()`](https://validate-hta.github.io/testhta/reference/set_time_horizon.md)
  : Set time horizon
- [`get_state_costs()`](https://validate-hta.github.io/testhta/reference/get_state_costs.md)
  : Getter for state costs
- [`get_state_utilities()`](https://validate-hta.github.io/testhta/reference/get_state_utilities.md)
  : Getter for state utilities
- [`get_transition_matrix()`](https://validate-hta.github.io/testhta/reference/get_transition_matrix.md)
  : Getter for transition probability matrix
- [`get_qalys()`](https://validate-hta.github.io/testhta/reference/get_qalys.md)
  : Getter for QALYs
- [`get_qalys_pp()`](https://validate-hta.github.io/testhta/reference/get_qalys_pp.md)
  : Getter for per-person QALYs
- [`get_costs()`](https://validate-hta.github.io/testhta/reference/get_costs.md)
  : Getter for costs
- [`get_costs_pp()`](https://validate-hta.github.io/testhta/reference/get_costs_pp.md)
  : Getter for per-person costs
- [`get_le()`](https://validate-hta.github.io/testhta/reference/get_le.md)
  : Getter for life expectancy (LE)
- [`get_le_pp()`](https://validate-hta.github.io/testhta/reference/get_le_pp.md)
  : Getter for per-person life expectancy (LE)
- [`get_icer()`](https://validate-hta.github.io/testhta/reference/get_icer.md)
  : Getter for ICER
- [`get_incremental_costs()`](https://validate-hta.github.io/testhta/reference/get_incremental_costs.md)
  : Getter for incremental costs
- [`get_incremental_qalys()`](https://validate-hta.github.io/testhta/reference/get_incremental_qalys.md)
  : Getter for incremental QALYs
- [`get_arm_names()`](https://validate-hta.github.io/testhta/reference/get_arm_names.md)
  : Getter for treatment arm names

## Example Case Study Model

The cohort Markov model engine and baseline dataset used as the
demonstration environment in the tutorial paper.

- [`ce_markov()`](https://validate-hta.github.io/testhta/reference/ce_markov.md)
  : Run cost-effectiveness Markov model
- [`p_matrix_cycle()`](https://validate-hta.github.io/testhta/reference/p_matrix_cycle.md)
  : Time-dependent probability matrix
- [`sample_psa_parameters()`](https://validate-hta.github.io/testhta/reference/sample_psa_parameters.md)
  : Sample probabilistic sensitivity analysis (PSA) parameters
- [`base_params`](https://validate-hta.github.io/testhta/reference/base_params.md)
  [`test_data`](https://validate-hta.github.io/testhta/reference/base_params.md)
  : Baseline parameters for the cohort Markov model case study
